lesson.title: Narrow procedural tasks
lesson.summary: Distinguish a genuinely narrow procedural task from a substantive personal decision.

prerequisites.reason: A procedural task does not bypass the gateway or its decision-influence analysis.

blocks: The **narrow procedural-task condition** concerns intended performance of a limited process step. 'Procedural' is not a label that can be pasted onto applicant evaluation or another substantive assessment.
Northbridge describes the exact operation, what it selects or changes, and what consequences follow. This lets a reviewer test narrowness rather than rely on a job title.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(a), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

blocks: Fictional case: a tool converts already supplied application files into a consistent format without choosing applicants or evaluating personal suitability. This illustrates a narrow-function hypothesis.
It is not an automatic legal conclusion. The system must meet the definition and relevant listed-use facts before a paragraph 3 derogation matters; the gateway and profiling rule still need evidence.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(a), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

blocks: Changed fact: conversion drops applicants based on predicted suitability. The operation now contains substantive evaluation and changes who reaches the reviewer.
A limited input or short output does not prove a narrow procedural task. Decision effects and actual evaluation matter. Reassess when features or integrations change.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(a), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

blocks: An assessment records the operation and the reason it satisfies a condition, the no-significant-risk analysis, and whether it performs personal profiling. Retain evidence of what happens on errors and downstream use.
If a supposedly narrow task's error removes an essential application from review, the gateway needs careful examination. Do not equate a small component with insignificant harm.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(a), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

questions.prompt: A tool merely reformats supplied files without assessing applicants. What is the appropriate approach?

options.blocks: Examine the narrow-task hypothesis and remaining tests
options.reason: The function supports a condition analysis, not automatic exemption.
Other functions and the gateway still matter.
The case expressly lacks that evaluative function.
